answer: A dune-like proof-of-stake registry can resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive rather than free. Each agent must lock a refundable bond and publish a beacon record linking its key to past work, so creating many fake identities means funding many bonds. Peers check the beacon history before trading: new keys with no work, no bond, or inconsistent quartz-like audit trails are treated as untrusted and given only tiny, rate-limited tasks. An attacker can still spawn identities, but each one costs capital and time, while honest agents reuse one established identity at no extra cost.
